GEORGIA BASELINE SGP ANALYSES

Methodology and results associated with Georgia Baseline SGP analyses

Damian W Betebenner
National Center for the Improvement of Educational Assessment
Atlanta, GA February 11th, 2015

RATIONALE FOR BASELINE ANALYSES

• Student growth percentiles are norm-referenced.

• For accountability purposes, Georgia desired a metric that
allowed for “all boats to rise” similar to criterion referenced
achievement.

• Following Massachusetts, Georgia began calculating baseline
referenced SGPs.

• The analyses were extended in 2013 to include measurement
error correction.

REQUIREMENTS FOR BASELINE ANALYSES
• Comparisons over time (column 2) require a time invariant scale.

• Improvement in percent pro cient requires a stable pro ciency
threshold.

• Baseline growth requires a stable scale since the coef cient
matrices utilize scale scores to reference quantile cuts.

• The vast majority of content area by grade analyses in MA and
GA support the hypothesis that the scales are well equated.

• MA (one example) and GA (~5 examples) show
abnormally large deviations from year to year.

SGP BASELINE ANALYSES
• Baseline analyses utilize multiple cohorts of students for each
analysis.

• For Biology the super cohort consist of 2007-2012 data including:

• 2007-2010 Grade 7 Science

• 2008-2011 Grade 8 Science

• 2009-2012 Biology

• A super-cohort is used to “average” any scale or population
abnormalities.
